I am giving this a Not Recommend for now in the interest that this game continues to improve. At launch, I refunded the game because of performance issues, but in its current state I believe that for casual players like me who just enjoy balancing supply chains and building a giant urban sprawl, this game is a good purchase on a sale. That being said, there are a couple annoying items that detract from the fun, most notably with managing zoning on specific tiles and not having a way to change out industry supply chains aside from demolishing over and over until you get the company (and product) you want. Overall if you're looking to upgrade from CS1 and aren't invested in modding, this is worth your time, but it still needs more improvements to be truly special. I am having fun. However, for every improvement and depth Cities Skyline 2 adds on top of Cities Skylines 1, it also seemingly removes control and buries information in abstract ways, removing agency from the player. This doesn't need to continue to be the case and I belive the current developers will make this game better.

I am one of the suckers who preordered the ultimate edition for this game, based on my 2000 hours on C:S1. I specifically built my PC with parts so I can run this game well. The game's launch was such a mess (graphic performance issues) I left it to rot in my steam library for nearly 2 years.

Now the game is playable but barely. Spend an hour more you'll find the bugs with simulation. The road tools and new graphics are a beautiful facade for a deeply flawed and shallow city simulation.

The devs disabled building abandonment mechanics altogether as a quick fix for deeper simulation bugs. This supposed "quick fix" was what I read in a patch notes posted four months ago by the devs, after becoming curious why none of my buildings were occupied. Let that sink in. A city sim with no abandonment mechanics for 4 months!

Yes, this is my bitter rant that I paid double the base price for a broken game. None of the DLCs in the ultimate edition have been released after delay after delay.

Moreover, coming to this store page I just watched the gameplay trailer full of promising mechanics and graphics, in a magical dejavu moment from SimCity 2013. I am deeply saddened for this franchise and the genre.

Cities 1 was a huge portion of my steam library's overall playtime, so I am utterly appalled by how amazingly Paradox managed to fuck up so severely and ruin literally everything that was great about the first game. The lies, deceit and general shadiness that Colossal and Paradox have displayed is sickening, the only updates Cities 2 receives now are minor patches and none of the modding support that was promised (and is still BEING promised) has been added. The fact they're adding even more DLC is the shitty cherry on top, given the fact that they're selling a 10 dollar pack of houses that a modder could've very easily added for free. I wish I hadn't invested in the deluxe edition because I feel utterly defrauded and shammed. Fuck you Paradox, yet again.

I had high hopes for Cities: Skylines 2, but a year after release, it's clear this sequel doesn't live up to its predecessor. Despite promises of improvements, the game still struggles with major performance issues. Even on high-end PCs, frame rates tank when your city starts to grow—a core part of the game!

The charm and efficiency of the original Cities: Skylines are completely missing here. The new mechanics feel half-baked, and there’s no real innovation to justify this game’s existence. Worse, the modding community—which kept the first game alive—is left fighting against a buggy foundation.
